records.previously_observed_photo_features: Well-displayed branched awned inflorescences, broad leaf blades, markedly hairy/papillose sheaths in closeups, and wetland edge habitat; multiple independent observations.
records.previously_unresolved_photo_features: Awn and papilla-based sheath hairs strongly favor Walter's barnyardgrass, but the critical lower floret lemma/awn origin, glume size and comparison with E. crus-galli are not fully measured.
reference_evidence: Diggs et al. (1999) regional Flora printed p.1266 staged register: papilla-based hispid leaf sheaths; often awned sterile/lower lemma; grass in wet habitat.

Go Botany Echinochloa key (2026): lower sheaths hispid with pustulose bases; lower nodes pubescent, E. crus-galli sheaths generally glabrous; upper lemma morphology differentiates E. muricata and related taxa.
FNA account mirrored by BioGator: spikelets 3–5 mm, lower lemma usually awned but sometimes short/awnless; rare glabrous lower sheaths.
records.taxon_and_character_reconciliation: Field QA already sees markedly hairy/papillose sheaths and awned heads, a strong lead; however, *rare glabrous E. walteri individuals* and awn variation mean sheath hair and long awns must not be absolute required filter states. Spikelet lemma apex and callus need measurement vs E. crus-galli and E. muricata.
records.required_same_local_specimen_evidence: Same Hays creekside plant: inner collar showing ligule absent, papilla-based sheath hair bases and nodes at 1 mm, two mature spikelets 3–5 mm excluding awn, awn base on lower lemma and upper lemma distal transition at 25×; compare E. crus-galli and E. muricata.
records.potential_false_exclusion_to_avoid: Awnless or nearly glabrous exceptional E. walteri is documented; do not false-exclude those unless more independent features rule them out.
records.occurrence_native_or_planted_context: Six prior Hays source observations, multiple wetland scenes; no Hays specimen voucher independently verified and county-level BONAP map cell unchecked.
records.next_useful_action: Very high value same-plant spikelet dissection plus measured sheath hair photo.

POWO 2026 and ITIS accept Polypogon viridis; Agrostis semiverticillata and Polypogon semiverticillatus are synonyms, not additional species.
FNA treatment reproduced Burke Herbarium: ligules up to about 5 mm (vs Diggs 2–7 mm), dense interrupted panicle and awnless glumes/lemmas.
records.taxon_and_character_reconciliation: Ligule lengths 2–7 mm (Diggs) versus ≤5 mm (FNA) overlap but published ranges differ; do not invent a fixed 5-mm cutoff. Long glume awns (Polypogon monspeliensis) are a useful contrast, but lack of awns cannot be reliably assessed in low-res heads.
records.required_same_local_specimen_evidence: Hays creekside same-specimen awnless glume/lemma macros (at least two spikelets, 1-mm scale), complete interrupted panicle, measured inner membranous ligule and decumbent rooted nodes; compare P. monspeliensis and Agrostis.
records.potential_false_exclusion_to_avoid: Synonym deduplication essential; no extra taxon for Agrostis semiverticillata. Preserve ligule range as nonexclusive.
records.occurrence_native_or_planted_context: Three historical Hays photos from wet rock/creek, no mature spikelet/ligule same plant proof, no Hays voucher.
